title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OWEN'S REUNION
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Owen Pike, thirty-eight, who hauls lobster traps in Rockland, Maine.
Owen liked his life. Then the invitation came. His twentieth high school reunion.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PHOTOS
segments.quote: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Owen looked up his old buddy Brad online. Boston. Big office. A car that costs more than a house.
Suddenly Owen's truck looked tired. So did Owen.
His boss, Captain Dot, seventy-one, saw his face and read him a line from Seneca, a Roman thinker:
It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
Owen put the phone down, and picked the rope back up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LEAK
segments.quote: Beware of little expenses. A small leak will sink a great ship.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Still, he wanted to look good. Fancy jacket. Rented sports car. Maybe a gold watch.
His wife Jen added it up on the fridge, next to her Ben Franklin magnet:
Beware of little expenses. A small leak will sink a great ship.
Owen laughed. He works on a boat. He knows about leaks. He cancelled the car.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE JACKET
segments.quote: Self-confidence is the first requisite to great undertakings.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: The night of the reunion, he almost stayed home.
Jen handed him his clean work jacket and a note in Samuel Johnson's words:
Self-confidence is the first requisite to great undertakings.
So Owen walked in as himself. Smelling only a little bit like bait.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BRAGGING
segments.quote: He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Everyone was bragging. Bigger homes. Bigger boats. Bigger everything.
Owen felt small, until he remembered a line from Epictetus, an old Greek teacher, that Dot keeps taped to her wheel:
He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
So he told them about sunrise on the water. Soon, half the room was listening.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: BRAD
segments.quote: Try not to become a man of success, but rather try to become a man of value.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: Late that night, Brad found him outside. Brad looked tired. Eighty-hour weeks. No time for anyone.
Brad said his first boss gave him a line from Albert Einstein, and he forgot it:
Try not to become a man of success, but rather try to become a man of value.
Owen said, come out on the boat tomorrow. Five a.m. Wear old shoes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SUNRISE
segments.quote: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: Brad showed up in loafers. He got wet. He laughed for the first time in years.
As the sun came up, Dot read one more, from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
Now Brad drives up one weekend a month. Same loafers. Still wet.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Want less. Watch the leaks. Be yourself. Count what you have. Be useful. Think happy.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Want less. Watch the little leaks. Show up as yourself. Count what you have. Aim to be useful. And think your way happy.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And please, never wear loafers on a boat.
